# UI guidelines — index

> **What this is.** The settled UI decisions, written down so they are followed rather than
> re-argued. Every rule here was decided by the owner; none of it is inferred from what the code
> happens to do today. Above all of them sits the noddo design system's own `SPEC.md`
> (`hris/styles/noddo/`, [`DESIGN_SYSTEM.md`](DESIGN_SYSTEM.md)): where a rule here and SPEC disagree,
> SPEC wins and the rule is changed.
>
> **Shelf: permanent.** This is `technical_documentation/`, so it is edited in place and outlives any
> programme. It is the answer half of `analysis/ui/` — that folder asks the questions and maps the
> variants, this one records what was chosen. When a question there is answered, the answer lands
> here and the question is struck.
>
> **The work of making the product match it** was the UI unification plan, closed on 2026-10-29 —
> the story is `HISTORY.md` § "UI consistency"; the places a rule was still untrue of a screen were built
> on 2026-10-30 (`HISTORY.md` § "Platform"), not walked yet. A rule
> can be settled here long before the screens obey it, and that is the normal state — **write the
> rule first, then close the gap**.

> **The designers read a copy.** `hris/design/rules/` is this folder, copied by
> `node design/sync-rules.mjs` (run in `hris/`) — run it after any edit here, or the designers work
> from the old rule. The protocol with them is `hris/design/HANDOFF.md`.

## How to use this

**Before building any screen**, read the file for what you are building. Before adding a variant —
another kebab icon, another empty state, another way of marking a required field — check whether the
answer is already here. It usually is now.

If a rule does not cover your case, that is a **question, not a licence**. Put it in
`NEED_TO_DISCUSS.md` rather than inventing an eighth variant; the whole reason this folder exists is
that fifteen screens each answered the same question privately.

## The three rules behind the rules

Everything in this folder follows from three positions, and quoting them is usually faster than
quoting the specific rule:

1. **One answer per question, in one place.** Five copies of `statusBadge` is not five decisions, it
   is one decision made five times and remembered differently. A rule that cannot be expressed as a
   shared component is a rule that will drift.
2. **A control that cannot work is not offered.** Not greyed with an unexplained tooltip, not
   rendered and refused on click — absent, or disabled with the reason on screen. The archived
   toggle that hides itself when nothing is archived is this rule, not a nicety.
3. **The interface does not claim more than it knows.** "Nothing here" and "we could not ask" are
   different screens. This is the same principle as the error formula
   (`technical_documentation/ERRORS.md`) applied to layout instead of to refusals.
